title: Looking back: the stories
hook: ten Gurus, the sakhis, the Khalsa's birth: which story stayed with you

segments.voice: Yesterday, bigana: Guru Arjan's line, no enemy and no stranger, and your line, no one is a stranger. Did you greet someone warmly? Today we start climbing to the lookout at the end of the year, and look back. Day three hundred twenty-six.

So, what have you actually learned on this path? Someone will ask it at dinner one day. You could list facts. Or you could tell them a story. A man who walked into a river and didn't come out for three days. A carpenter's plain bread, and a rich man's feast. A boy who told his father, no one is more worthy than you. A sword drawn before a crowd, and five people who stood up. A faith often travels in its stories more than its facts. This week, we look back at the whole year, and we start with them. Today: looking back.
screen: `WHAT HAVE YOU LEARNED?` → `A RIVER, A LOAF, A SWORD.` → `THE STORIES FIRST.`

segments.voice: Camp two was the stories, and they came in a line of ten Gurus. Guru Nanak, three days in the river Bein, coming out to say there is no Hindu and no Muslim. Eating Bhai Lalo's honest bread and refusing Malik Bhago's feast. Walking the world with Mardana and his rabab, then farming at Kartarpur. Guru Angad, shaping the Gurmukhi letters, while Mata Khivi ran the kitchen. Guru Amar Das, the old man who carried water before dawn, and who, the story goes, asked everyone, even an emperor, to eat in the langar first. Guru Ram Das, digging the pool at Amritsar. Guru Arjan, building a temple with four doors and gathering the hymns into one book, then dying in custody in Lahore, remembered by Sikhs as a martyr. Guru Hargobind, wearing two swords. Guru Har Rai and his herb garden. Guru Har Krishan, a child nursing the sick in Delhi. Guru Tegh Bahadur, giving his life for the freedom of people of another faith. And Guru Gobind Singh: Vaisakhi, 1699, the sword, the five beloved, sugar stirred into water in an iron bowl, and the Guru asking the five to initiate him. And at the end, in 1708, the Guru passing the Guruship to the Granth. The word for these stories is sakhi. A sakhi is a story of the Gurus, and the word is usually traced to an old word for a witness. That's what a good sakhi does. It doesn't just inform you. It stands beside you as a witness when you need it: at a table where someone's being left out, at a moment you want to cheat, on a day you need courage. So the question today isn't which story is most important. It's which one stayed with you.
screen: `TEN GURUS, ONE LINE.` · `NANAK TO GOBIND SINGH.` · `THE GURU BECOMES THE GRANTH.` · `A SAKHI IS A WITNESS.` · then, large: `WHICH STORY STAYED?`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: retell one story aloud. Settle, and breathe. Let the stories drift past, and wait for the one that tugs at you. Don't pick the one you think you should. Pick the one that stayed. Now tell it, out loud if you can, softly, in your own words, as if to a child. It's fine to forget details. Just tell what happened and why it matters to you. Then sit with it for a while in the quiet. The bell holds the time.
Looking back. The year's stories: ten Gurus, the sakhis, the Khalsa's birth, and the one that stayed with you.
Your line: which story stayed. Today, tell that story to one person, at a meal, on a call, or in a message. Day three hundred twenty-six.

howItsDone: Sikh families tell sakhis, stories of the Gurus, to children at home and in gurdwara classes, and katha (explanation) in the gurdwara often retells a sakhi alongside the day's hymn.

match.prompt: who's in the story — tap the pairs.

myth: Guru Nanak disappeared into the river Bein for three days
he came out saying there is no Hindu and no Muslim.
Guru Tegh Bahadur gave his life only to protect Sikhs
he gave it for the freedom of people of another faith, the pandits of Kashmir.
the Guruship passed to the Granth in 1708
Guru Gobind Singh told the Sikhs the Guru is the Granth.

fork.setup: Vaisakhi, 1699. the five have been initiated with amrit. what does Guru Gobind Singh do next?
options: he takes his seat as their commander.
he asks the five to initiate him too.
he sends them home to preach.
fork.reveal: the Guru became the disciple: he asked the five to give him amrit as well.

original.note: Gurmukhi: sakhi, a story of the Gurus; linked to an old word for a witness.

trapdoor: what you thought: the stories are Sikh history.
what it means: a sakhi is a story that stands beside you like a witness, when you need it.
what a scholar hears: many sakhis come from the janamsakhis, collections compiled after Guru Nanak's time; historians read them as devotion as well as history.
